chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Get married and get (others) married. Indeed, among the good fortune of a Muslim is spending on the price of an unmarried woman/widow. There is nothing more beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, than a household that prospers in Islam through marriage; and there is nothing more hateful to God, Mighty and Majestic, than a household that is ruined in Islam through separation' — meaning divorce.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, emphasized divorce and repeated speech concerning it because of His hatred of separation.'

key_terms.أَيِّمَةٍ: An unmarried or widowed woman; spending on facilitating her marriage is considered meritorious
key_terms.الطَّلَاقُ: Divorce — specifically the pronouncement of marital dissolution; here clarified as what is meant by 'al-furqah'
key_terms.النِّكَاحُ: Marriage — the Islamic legal contract of matrimony, considered among the most beloved institutions to God
key_terms.الْفُرْقَةُ: Separation/divorce — the dissolution of marriage, considered among the most hated acts to God
key_terms.وَكَّدَ: To emphasize/make firm; used to explain why the Quran's divorce rules are detailed and stringent

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the virtue of marriage and the dislike of divorce in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a prophetic tradition urging Muslims to marry and facilitate the marriages of others, with the Prophet declaring marriage to be among the greatest goods and divorce among the most detested acts before God. The Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides an explanatory comment, noting that the elaborate rulings on divorce in the Quran reflect God's profound dislike of marital separation. Delivered within the context of early Islamic community building, this teaching addressed communities where marriage was central to social stability and religious identity, while 'ayyimah' (unmarried/widowed women) represented a vulnerable social category whose care was a communal responsibility.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Safwan Bin Mihran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Get married (yourself)! Get (children) married off! Indeed, from the good fortune of a Muslim person is expenditure of the price (of marrying a) widow, and there is nothing more Beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than a house populated in Al-Islam with the marriage, and there is nothing more Hateful to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than a house which is ruined in Al-Islam with the separation, meaning the divorce’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Emphasised regarding the divorce and repeated His<sup>azwj</sup> Speech with regards to it of His<sup>azwj</sup> Hatred for the separation’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Safwan ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘It is of the share of good fortune of a Muslim that female members of his family find marriage early on and there is nothing more beloved to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, than a home that is established in Islam with marriage and there is nothing more hated to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, than a home that is destroyed in Islam because of division, - divorce.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has stressed on His hating divorce in repeated ways because of His extreme dislike of division.’”
